title: POC customer activation orbit plan
body:
One-line summary: lightweight, predictable 6-week POC plan to validate latency and cost targets for customer X's chat assistant and establish a production-ready deployment path (hosted -> dedicated -> private as needed).

Context and intent:
- Customer X needs a fast timeline (6 weeks) to decide on Dedicated vs Hosted for a high-throughput chat service (peak 250 qps, tail latency target 200ms p95).
- This doc is the working sprint canvas, task tracker, workshop agenda, and high-level handoff runbook. Keep it blunt and actionable.
- Current constraints: customer cannot share full production data, but will provide a 10k-sample pseudo-production prompt set and schema for anonymized records.

Goals and success criteria (measurable):
1) Functional baseline: integrated Redwood SDK + sample app + auth within week 1. (Owner: Priya)
2) Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for 512-token avg response on dedicated-small config OR hosted equivalent cost < $0.002/token. (Owner: Diego)
3) Cost projection: unit cost estimate and 30-day simulated spend report by week 4. (Owner: Maya)
4) Quality gate: conversation coherence >= 0.75 on holdout eval (customer labels) and <5% hallucination rate on named-entity prompts. (Owner: Samir)
5) Runbook + handoff: documented deployment steps, rollback, and monitoring thresholds by week 6. (Owner: Eleni)

High-level timeline (orbit weeks) - target dates for a Jan start:
- Orbit 0 (Week 0) - 2025-01-13 to 2025-01-19: kickoff, data handoff, scaffold app repo, security checklist, access to test infra
- Orbit 1 (Week 1) - 2025-01-20 to 2025-01-26: integration + smoke testing, first latency runs on hosted catalog model
- Orbit 2 (Week 2) - 2025-01-27 to 2025-02-02: dedicated capacity proof (small pool), batching/kv-cache experiments, initial cost model
- Orbit 3 (Week 3) - 2025-02-03 to 2025-02-09: quality evals, prompt set regression, short workshop with CS/Eng to review findings
- Orbit 4 (Week 4) - 2025-02-10 to 2025-02-16: scale tests (QPS ramp), resiliency checks (region failover simulation)
- Orbit 5 (Week 5) - 2025-02-17 to 2025-02-23: finalize cost-performance tradeoffs, draft recommended deployment blueprint
- Orbit 6 (Week 6) - 2025-02-24 to 2025-03-02: runbook delivery + executive review + decision milestone

Sprint board (kanban columns) - suggested rapid cadence:
- Backlog: research spikes, questions to customer
- Ready: tickets with acceptance criteria and dataset links
- In progress: active integrations, infra provisioning, evals
- Blocked: anything waiting on customer data or approvals
- Review: experiments/PRs awaiting signoff
- Done: merged, documented, smoke-tested

Task tracker (top-level tasks — each becomes linear/Jira ticket JIRA-ENG-xxxx):
- KICK-01: Customer kickoff (agenda + success criteria) — Owner: Maya — Due: 2025-01-15 — Status: done
- INF-10: Provision dedicated-small GPU pool (2x A10 equivalent) in staging region — Owner: Diego — Due: 2025-01-22 — Status: in_progress
- APP-03: Integrate Redwood SDK into customer sample app + CI smoke tests — Owner: Priya — Due: 2025-01-24 — Status: in_progress
- DATA-04: Validate anonymized prompt set; create holdout splits and eval harness — Owner: Samir — Due: 2025-01-25 — Status: ready
- EVAL-07: Baseline latency/cost runs on hosted LLM-2-small (50 runs, varying seq lengths) — Owner: Diego — Due: 2025-01-28 — Status: ready
- PERF-09: KV cache/batching experiments and recommended policy — Owner: Diego — Due: 2025-02-05 — Status: backlog
- QA-11: Label subset of 500 conversations for hallucination checks — Owner: Customer X / CS liaison — Due: 2025-02-02 — Status: blocked
- RUN-12: Draft deployment runbook + rollback steps — Owner: Eleni — Due: 2025-02-27 — Status: backlog

Acceptance tests (how we decide pass/fail):
- Integration smoke: API keys rotate, SDK auth works, sample app gets 200 OK for generation endpoint on CI with sample prompt.
- Latency test: p95 measured over 1,000 requests with realistic inter-arrival times. If p95 > 400ms, fail and iterate kernel/batching.
- Cost sim: run synthetic load for 72 hours against projected traffic pattern, produce per-token and per-request cost. If projected monthly cost > customer budget threshold, propose quantization or routing to cheaper variant.
- Quality: run holdout set and compute coherence/hallucination metrics. If hallucination > 7%, mark as quality risk and escalate to model/retry policy team.

Workshop agenda (60–90m technical onboarding session, week 3):
- 0–10m: Goals, definitions, and success criteria (Maya)
- 10–25m: Data & privacy constraints + anonymization checklist (Customer + Samir)
- 25–45m: Architecture walk: hosted vs dedicated vs private with cost/latency tradeoffs (Diego)
- 45–65m: Live demo: sample app + tracing + console walkthrough (Priya)
- 65–80m: Open issues and decisions: observability retention, SLO thresholds, rollout policy (all)
- 80–90m: Next steps and owners

Runbook sketch (hand-off friendly):
- Pre-reqs: customer IAM, test dataset upload location, dedicated pool sizing decision, KMS key if using Private
- Provision: terraform module id tpl-deploy/poc-dedicated-small (link in ticket)
- Deploy: 1) push model pin to catalog (safe tag), 2) configure autoscale floor to 2 GPUs, 3) enable prefix caching for session tokens
- Monitoring: enable token-level tracing, route errors to #prod-alerts, set p95 and error-rate alarms
- Rollback: scale to hosted-fallback route + gradual traffic shift over 5 minutes, notify on-call

Risks and mitigations (working list):
- RISK: Customer's anonymized set under-represents long-tail prompts. MITIGATION: add synthetic long-tail augmentation and schedule second eval before final decision. Owner: Samir
- RISK: Dedicated pool warmup increases tail latency on first requests. MITIGATION: use warmup traffic and pre-fill KV cache during ramp windows. Owner: Diego
- RISK: Cost exceeds expectations when scaled. MITIGATION: quantize to int8/4-bit variants and test accuracy delta; enable intelligent routing to cheaper variants when non-critical. Owner: Maya

Open questions (to capture during kickoff/workshop):
- What is definitive production qps/p95 expectation at 99% confidence?
- Can customer provide sample SLO SLA language to align monitoring thresholds?
- Any compliance requirements that force Private deployment?

Notes to self and scratch ideas:
- Try 512-token avg vs 256-token avg during latency runs; results differ a lot with tokenizer overhead.
- We should capture token distribution histogram from their data to tune batch sizes.
- Consider short-lived canary with function-calls enabled to emulate tool usage if customer plans to use retrieval.

Deliverables by orbit end:
- Orbit 1: scaffold repo, CI smoke, hosted baseline report
- Orbit 3: dedicated baseline, initial quality eval, workshop slides + recording
- Orbit 5: scaled stress report, final cost model, recommended blueprint with tradeoffs
- Orbit 6: runbook + executive summary for customer decision

Communication plan:
- Weekly async status in #se-poc-cadet on Fridays; include 3 bullets (progress, blockers, ask)
- Biweekly demo + decision sync with customer execs (calendar invite owner: Maya)

References and quick links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (POC scoring rubric)
- Jira epic: JIRA-ENG-7812
- Starter app repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-starter-kit/pull/58

Next immediate actions (today):
1) Send dataset upload instructions to customer (Maya) — target: EOD 2025-01-10
2) Diego to start infra provisioning ticket (INF-10) and share ETA — target: 2025-01-14
3) Priya to open PR with CI smoke tests (APP-03) — target: 2025-01-13

Small checklist for handoff to solutions ops:
- Confirm tagging policy for model variants (who approves safe-tag?)
- Attach cost simulation spreadsheet to JIRA epic
- Add runbook draft to Confluence and link in final PR

If anything needs to be moved to a formal playbook, flag under 'formalize' label. This doc remains the working orbit plan; expect many small edits and add tickets rather than large doc rewrites.
